scope: Bounded primary-source pass. PDF files are the exact arXiv versions named below; adjacent TXT files are pypdf text extractions. The candidate claim was supplied by the coordinator and was not proof-checked here.

sources.title: Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
sources.exact_interface: One fixed channel broadcasts two input states as both output marginals iff the states commute; the common-channel requirement is explicit. No approximate stability rate.
sources.locations: PDF pp. 3-9 (broadcasting definition and iff statement, pp. 3-4; converse proof, pp. 8-9).

sources.title: No-local-broadcasting theorem for quantum correlations
sources.exact_interface: A bipartite state is locally broadcastable by local maps on both parties iff it is classical-classical; the paper also characterizes equality of total mutual information under local broadcasting.
sources.locations: PDF p. 5, Theorem 3; PDF pp. 6-7, Theorems 4-5; Theorem 4 is the mutual-information formulation.

sources.title: Local Broadcasting of Quantum Correlations
sources.publication: Chapter in Lectures on General Quantum Correlations and Their Applications (2017)
sources.exact_interface: For one fixed rho_AB, local broadcasting by B is possible iff rho_AB is classical on B (Theorem 5). The chapter defines state-specific EB and broadcast fidelities, relates discord by D(A|B)>=-2 log2(Fmax), and states that average mutual-information loss converges to discord as output count grows.
sources.locations: PDF p. 6, Theorem 5; PDF p. 8, Eqs. (31)-(35); PDF p. 9, Eq. (36) and following limit statement.

sources.title: Hierarchy of efficiently computable and faithful lower bounds to quantum discord
sources.exact_interface: For a channel with a k-Bose-symmetric extension (output supported in the fully symmetric subspace), one EB channel approximates it uniformly over all finite reference extensions with half trace distance <=dim(B)/k. A state-specific fidelity corollary loses sqrt(2 dim(B)/k).
sources.locations: PDF p. 3, Eq. (4) and surrounding statement; PDF p. 7, Theorem 1.

sources.title: On quantum estimation, quantum cloning and finite quantum de Finetti theorems
sources.exact_interface: For a permutation-invariant M-output broadcast channel, a common measure-and-prepare channel approximates its k-output restriction in diamond norm by <=2 d^2 k/M; if the output lies in the fully symmetric subspace, the bound is <=2 d k/M. At k=1 the marginal is EB.

sources.title: Approximate broadcasting of quantum correlations
sources.exact_interface: Theorem 5 gives an SDP for optimal symmetric unilocal n-broadcasting fidelity of one bipartite state. Theorem 12 gives an SDP for one symmetric broadcast channel maximizing prior-weighted average fidelity over a finite ensemble of unentangled input states.
sources.locations: PDF p. 5, Theorem 5; PDF p. 8, Eqs. (26)-(29) and Theorem 12.
